title: Text to Slug Converter: Create URL-Friendly Slugs Online Free
description: Free online slug generator to convert titles into clean, URL-friendly slugs for WordPress, blogs and CMS systems. Private, instant, in your browser.

sections.heading: Slugs Are How URLs Get Legible
paragraphs: A clean slug turns "How to Merge PDF Files — A Complete Guide" into /how-to-merge-pdf-files, readable by humans, parseable by machines and indexed kindly by search engines. [text-to-slug:Generating slugs] from titles is the daily ritual of every CMS editor.
WordPress, Shopify, Hugo and hand-rolled routes all share the same slug conventions.
ChooseTools converts text to slugs locally in your browser, honoring separators and casing options.

sections.heading: How to Convert a Title Into a Slug
paragraphs: From headline to permalink in a click.
Paste your title or phrase and the tool lowers, strips and hyphenates it into a clean slug. Choose separator style (hyphens, underscores) and casing (lower, lowerCamel).
The output is ready to paste into your editing screen without manual cleanup.
Adjusting one option re-renders the slug instantly, so matching your CMS conventions is trivial.

sections.heading: Why Clean URLs Matter for SEO and Usability
paragraphs: Search engines parse meaningful slugs for context; readers share them reliably; analytics report them legibly.
Predictable permalinks survive imports and migrations without drift.
Pay the slug attention and your URL architecture repays in structure.
Human-readable URLs also inspire more clicks when shared in print, on email or in chat, because the destination is obvious at a glance.

sections.heading: National Characters and the Slug Edge Cases
paragraphs: Accented and non-Latin characters need transliteration rules to become URL-safe Latin.
The converter handles such edge cases so titles with á, é, ü and lookalikes still produce tidy slugs.
Punctuation, quotes and spaces collapse to safe separators.
This normalization prevents the long, broken, percent-encoded strings that break links and look unprofessional.

sections.heading: Slug Best Practices for Editors
paragraphs: Keep slugs short but descriptive: a few meaningful keywords beat a full sentence, and they read better in search results and browser tabs.
Avoid stop words such as the, of and and where they add no distinguishing value, since they waste characters and dilute the signal.
Use lowercase permanently once published, because changing a slug later breaks existing links and damages accumulated search authority.
Match your CMS's convention, typically hyphens for WordPress and Jekyll, while some frameworks prefer underscores or camelCase, which the tool lets you select directly.

sections.heading: SEO Consequences of Poor Slugs
paragraphs: Search engines weigh the URL as a relevance signal, and a slug containing the primary keyword strengthens the page's topical clarity for that query.
Auto-generated slugs from titles often include numbers or fragments, such as post-title-2024-06, which add no value and waste the most visible keyword space in a results page.
Session parameters and machine-generated identifiers make URLs harder to read, share and remember, discouraging the manual sharing that drives real traffic.
Investing seconds in a clean slug at publish time prevents years of mediocre performance and broken links later.

sections.heading: Transliteration and Multilingual Titles
paragraphs: Titles in German, French, Spanish and many other languages carry diacritics that browsers handle awkwardly in URLs. Converting ü to ue or retaining u depends on the language and your editorial preference, and the tool applies sensible defaults.
For non-Latin scripts such as Cyrillic, Arabic or Greek, a phonetic transliteration produces an English-readable slug that still matches the topic for Latin-script readers.
Consistent transliteration rules matter for multilingual sites where a Spanish slug and an English slug should both feel natural and predictable.
You can also choose to keep or drop diacritics to match your brand's conventions, giving multilingual publishers full control over how their URLs read.

sections.heading: How a Slug Fits Into Your URL Structure
paragraphs: The slug is the final segment of a larger URL path, such as /blog/category-name/slug, and it carries the most specific identifying information for the page.
A thoughtful slug hierarchy, with category then post, helps both users and search engines understand where a page sits in your site.
Keeping slugs stable after publication is critical, since each one anchors bookmarks, backlinks and search rankings that take months to accumulate.
When you must change a slug, a redirect preserves most of the value, but avoiding the change altogether is always better.

faqs.q: Which characters are removed when making a slug?
faqs.a: Punctuation, quotes and symbols are stripped or replaced with safe separators, and accented characters are transliterated to URL-safe letters.

faqs.q: Can I choose hyphens or underscores as separators?
faqs.a: Yes. Separator style and casing options let you match your CMS or framework's slug conventions exactly.
Yes. Conversion runs entirely in your browser with no uploads, no accounts and no server-side processing.

faqs.q: Can I use the same slug across different CMS platforms?
faqs.a: Yes. The generated slug is a standard URL-safe string, so it works in WordPress, Shopify, Hugo and most other publishing systems without modification.
